title: Present tense of `tag-`
summary: Core present-tense subject-marker patterns currently taught in the course.

rows.label: I
rows.note: Use `waan` with a first-person present-tense action from the greetings context.

rows.label: You
rows.note: Use `waad` for `you`, then keep the sentence in the leave-taking context.

rows.label: He
rows.note: Use `wuu` with a family check-in action from the early conversation lessons.

rows.label: She
rows.note: Use `way` for `she` with the introduction phrase.

rows.label: We (including you)
rows.note: Use `waynu` when `we` includes the person you are speaking to.

rows.label: We (not including you)
rows.prompt: We are going, not including you.
rows.note: Use `waannu` when `we` does not include the person you are speaking to.

rows.label: You all
rows.note: Use `waydin` for `you all` with a names/introduction action.

rows.label: They
rows.note: Use `way` for `they` with a leave-taking phrase.

title: Past tense of `yimi`
summary: Core past-tense verb-form patterns currently taught in the course.

rows.label: I
rows.note: Use the past form with the village-stay context.

rows.label: You
rows.note: Use the past form with a communication lesson noun.

rows.label: He
rows.note: Use the past form with `safarka` from the journey lessons.

rows.label: She
rows.note: Use the past form with the village-stay context.

rows.label: We
rows.note: Use the past form with the journey context.

rows.label: You all
rows.note: Use the past form with the village-stay context.

rows.label: They
rows.note: Use the past form with `tuulada` and `ka`.
